passage: Right, I'm Nikita. When I confronted Joseph about copying, I had my speech about honesty ready. Then he snapped, “You don't know what it's like,” and I heard the rest: his father checks every mark on the sheet and won't speak for a day if it drops. That changed things, but not everything. I told him I understood the pressure, and that the copying still had to stop, because it wasn't fair to him or to the class. He looked at me as if I'd slapped him. Then I said, “What if we ask Mr Iyer about extra classes, and I come along?” We went on Thursday. Mr Iyer gave him a slot on Tuesdays and Fridays. My little brother says I'm the bossiest didi ever, but this wasn't bossing. The problem was never only cheating; it was fear.

qa.q: What does Joseph's father do when a mark drops?
qa.a: His father checks every mark on the sheet and won't speak for a day if it drops.

qa.q: How did Joseph feel when Nikita said the copying still had to stop?

Joseph could talk to the school counsellor and, if he agrees, to his parents about the pressure he feels at home.

qa.q: How might Mr Iyer see Joseph asking for extra classes?
qa.a: Mr Iyer probably sees it as a good sign, a student wanting to learn instead of hiding, and he offers regular slots.

I'm Bidisha, and I sit behind Mohit and Arvind. Mohit had been angry with Arvind for a week, ever since he saw him copying in the maths test. I heard him say, “I'm telling Sir if you do it again.”
Then on Friday something changed. They were talking by the water cooler, and Arvind was crying, which I'd never seen. I caught bits: his father had said that if he failed maths again, he'd be sent to his uncle's town for school. He'd been failing since August and was too scared to say.
Mohit didn't back down about the copying. I heard him say, “You still have to stop. But you need help, not a cheat sheet.” After school he went with Arvind to Sir, not to report him, but to ask about the free remedial classes on Tuesdays.
On Tuesday I saw them both in the remedial room. Arvind had his notebook open. Mohit was there too, doing his own homework, just keeping him company.

qa.q: What did Mohit and Arvind ask Sir about?
qa.a: The free remedial classes on Tuesdays.

qa.q: What might Mohit have been feeling when Arvind cried?
qa.a: Mohit was probably surprised and sympathetic, his anger softening into concern, though he still felt the copying had to stop.

qa.q: What else could help Arvind besides the remedial classes?
qa.a: Talking with a teacher or counsellor about the pressure at home, so an adult can help his father understand.

qa.q: How does the change look to Bidisha?
qa.a: Bidisha sees a friendship shift from anger to support, with Mohit even sitting in the remedial room for company.

grounding: A classmate sees a teen learn his friend cheated under heavy pressure from home, still insist he stop, and help him ask for tutoring.

Monday: Omkar sees Sagar copy from notes in his lap during the physics test. That evening Omkar decides: Sagar stops, or Omkar goes to Minakshi Ma'am.
Wednesday: Omkar confronts him at the cycle stand. Sagar snaps, then goes quiet and admits it. His parents want him to top the class because his elder brother did; his father checks every mark and shouts over a single mistake. He's been sleeping four hours to keep up and is still falling behind.
Omkar's anger shifts. He still says, “You have to stop copying.” But now he adds, “And you need real help with physics, not just pressure.”
Friday: Omkar goes with Sagar to Minakshi Ma'am. Sagar tells her about the copying himself, and about needing help. She arranges extra tutoring after school and says she will talk to his parents about expectations.
The next Monday: Sagar sits the physics retest with no notes.

How did Omkar's feelings change on Wednesday?

qa.q: What else could Omkar do to support Sagar in the coming weeks?

qa.a: Sagar was probably scared but relieved not to go alone, and to finally say what the pressure had been doing.
